approach: In `run_job` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs), the slot is taken at line 1439 (`st.started += 1`) after the checks at 1430-1438, and nothing gives it back. In the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm (line 1537), take the state lock and set `st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1)` before returning `RunStep::NeedsAccepting`. The read and run costs are already added to the budget (lines 1462 and 1527) and stay. The JobLimit check and the Passed, Held, Failed and budget arms are untouched. The other readers of `st.started` (lines 1889, 2008, 2555, 2896) then see the freed slot unchanged. Add one regression test with the shared `Stub` and `max_jobs: 1`. Update the job-limit wording in the module docs, the `Limits::max_jobs` doc, and the help text in main.rs. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Give the slot back in the `run.needs_accepting` arm of `run_job` with a saturating decrement of `st.started` under the state lock.
decisions.reason: `run_job` is the only place that takes a slot (line 1439) and the only place that sees a NeedsAccepting outcome (line 1537). The real source is RealSteps::run (drain.rs ~3572 sets needs_accepting: true); the test Stub returns the same Run shape. One change covers a re-read, a first read and an approved job alike, and keeps every reader of `st.started` in step.

rejected.option: Check `started >= max_jobs` and increment only after the run ends in a counted outcome.
rejected.why: A parallel worker could then start more jobs than the limit while this one is in flight. The slot has to be held during the job.
Needs-accepting arises inside `steps.run` (line 1523), not in the `Source::Reread` branch (line 1445). The root-cause default says to fix the slot counting, not one source.

rejected.option: Add a separate counter of free slots.
rejected.why: Lines 1889, 2008, 2555 and 2896 all read `st.started`; a second counter would need all of them changed.

rejected.option: Also release the slot for Held, budget-short and Failed outcomes.
rejected.why: Out of scope: the request says the other outcomes keep counting.

decisions.choice: Leave the budget accounting alone: `st.budget.add(read.cost)` (1462) and `st.budget.add(run.cost)` (1527) stay.
decisions.reason: The money was spent on model calls, and the out-of-scope list keeps spend counted against the budget.

rejected.option: Refund the cost of the needs-accepting attempt.
rejected.why: The spend is real; refunding would let a batch overspend.

decisions.choice: Write the regression test with the shared `Stub` (needs_accepting = ["a"]) instead of a new inline Steps impl.
decisions.reason: `Stub::run` already returns needs_accepting for a named job and lets b land through `outcomes`; `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop` shows the `max_jobs: 1` pattern. It is the smallest test, and the counter logic under test stays in production `run_job`.

rejected.option: Copy the inline `Unaccepted` struct used by the existing needs-accepting test.
rejected.why: More code for the same seam, and it uses read-ahead items.

files.purpose: In `run_job`'s `run.needs_accepting` arm, give the slot back with a saturating decrement of `st.started` under the state lock. Update the module docs (configuration-change bullet ~176-181) and the `Limits::max_jobs` doc (~253) to say such a re-read does not count toward the job limit.
Add `a_needs_accepting_reread_does_not_use_a_job_slot` after `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop` (~1441). No existing test is edited.
Update the `job limit` stop-reasons line (~256) and the `--job-limit` doc (~288) to say a needs-accepting re-read is not counted.
Add a Fixed entry under [Unreleased]: a re-read that ends as needs accepting no longer uses a --job-limit slot, and the drain goes on to the next item.

steps: In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs `run_job`, in the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm (line 1537), before `RunStep::NeedsAccepting` is returned, lock the state (`self.st()`) and set `st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1)`. Add a comment: a re-read that only needs accepting leaves the item queued and spends money but no job slot. Do not touch the JobLimit check at 1433 or the other arms.

In crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs add `a_needs_accepting_reread_does_not_use_a_job_slot` after `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop`: build `Stub { items: vec!["a","b"], needs_accepting: vec!["a"], outcomes: passing(), ratings: RefCell::new(vec![3]), ..Stub::default() }` (match the field shapes the neighbouring tests use), call `drain::drain(&stub, Limits { max_jobs: 1, ..limits(9.0) }, &Quiet)`, and assert `report.jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting"`, `report.landed == 1`, `report.stop != Stop::JobLimit`, that the log has `run a`, `run b` and `land b` in that order with one `run a`, and that a is still queued.

Update docs: in drain.rs module docs (configuration-change bullet ~176-181) add that such a re-read does not count toward `--job-limit`; update the `Limits::max_jobs` doc (~253) the same way; in main.rs update the `job limit` stop-reasons line (~256) and the `--job-limit` doc comment (~288). Use the phrase `does not count`.

Add a `### Fixed` entry (create the heading if it is not in Unreleased) to CHANGELOG.md under `## [Unreleased]`, naming the cause (the slot was taken before the read and never given back) and the effect.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. For criterion 2, remove the decrement briefly, confirm the new test fails with `Stop::JobLimit` and `landed == 0`, report that, and restore it.

risks.risk: The drain might end with `Stop::JobLimit` after b lands, so the `stop != JobLimit` assertion fails for a reason other than the counter. I saw that JobLimit comes only from an item meeting the limit at `run_job` (line 1433), but I did not trace the end-of-queue path and cannot run the test.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs the test. If the stop is something else (for example queue empty), assert that stop exactly. The assertions that matter are `landed == 1` and `stop != Stop::JobLimit`.

risks.risk: A later pass in the same drain (a wave, a restart) could pick the needs-accepting item up again and loop on it, because its attempt no longer takes a slot.
risks.mitigation: `finish` passes the item over (~2411) and `attempts` returns after one NeedsAccepting. The new test checks the log has exactly one `run a`. The existing needs-accepting test also asserts a single `run a`.

risks.risk: Underflow of `st.started` if the decrement ran without a matching increment.
risks.mitigation: The arm is reached only after `st.started += 1` in the same call (line 1439), and the decrement is `saturating_sub(1)`.

risks.risk: New doc wording trips a doc or boundary scan test.
risks.mitigation: Keep the wording plain with no banned words, and run `cargo test --locked` for the whole workspace.

demonstrations.method: Run the new test. It calls the production `drain::drain` with `Limits { max_jobs: 1, ..limits(9.0) }` and checks the report.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. It asserts `report.jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting"`, `report.landed == 1`, `report.stop != Stop::JobLimit`, and that the stub log has `run a`, then `run b`, then `land b`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the decrement, `st.started` is 1 after a, so b's `run_job` returns `RunStep::JobLimit` at line 1433. The drain stops with `Stop::JobLimit` and `landed == 0`, so the landed and stop assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `drain::drain(&dyn Steps, Limits, &Ui)`, which reaches `run_job`. Fixture: the existing `Stub` in tests/drain.rs, injected as `&stub`, with items a and b, `needs_accepting: vec!["a"]`, `outcomes: passing()` and `ratings: RefCell::new(vec![3])`. The stub only returns the `Run` the real step would; the slot counting runs in production `run_job`. Exists: I read `Stub::run` (~223) and `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop` (~1422). Step 2 adds only the test function.

demonstrations.method: Temporarily remove the decrement in the working tree, run the new test and see it fail, then restore the decrement and see it pass. The failing run is shown by the producer in its report. The verifier can repeat it, or read that the test's assertions (`landed == 1`, `stop != Stop::JobLimit`) cannot hold under the old counter.
demonstrations.observes: With the decrement removed the test fails with `landed == 0` and `Stop::JobLimit`. With it restored the test passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: The old counter keeps the slot, so b is refused at line 1433 and the landed and stop assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: `drain::drain` with the `Stub` injected as `&stub`. Exists today. The removal is a temporary edit to `run_job` made by the producer in step 5, not a double.

demonstrations.observes: In the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm of `run_job`, the diff shows a lock of the state (`self.st()`) and `st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1)`. The `if st.started >= self.limits.max_jobs` check, the `st.started += 1` line, and the Passed, Held and `other` arms show no change.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole drain test file, then read the diff of tests/drain.rs to check that it only adds lines.
demonstrations.observes: `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop`, `an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal`, `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure`, `a_reread_whose_scope_changed_is_left_for_a_person_and_is_not_a_failure` and `passed_over_item_is_logged_once_with_its_reason` all pass. `git diff -- crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs` shows no removed `assert` lines.
